summary: commonweb-flow pulls install-scripted tarball from non-registry host at install time
details: commonweb-flow@99.99.99 declares a dependency resolved via a direct HTTPS URL to a non-registry host: "linker-event-header-serial": "https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/linker-event-header-serial". The shipped npm-shrinkwrap.json pins that same URL with "hasInstallScript": true, so on `npm install` npm downloads that tarball and executes its lifecycle scripts on the installer's machine. The wrapper itself has placeholder metadata (author "Package Registry", description "Generated package", repository github.com/example/commonweb-flow) and version 99.99.99, the canonical high-version shape used to shadow an internal package name via dependency confusion. The wrapper has no documented build reason for an external artifact host, and the fetched tarball's contents are attacker-controlled — whoever operates artifacts.yosiroute.com obtains arbitrary code execution on any host that installs this package.
